questions.q: The three processes of memory per the page are:
questions.exp: Processes of memory: encoding (registration), consolidation (storage) and retrieval. (Book p569)

questions.q: Per the old duration table, which store has NO storage and is exemplified by recalling a phone number within 1 minute?
questions.exp: Duration table: immediate/working memory = no storage, e.g. recalling a phone number within 1 min; short term/recent = hippocampus storage, e.g. recalling breakfast; long term = neocortex, e.g. recalling something from distant past. (Book p569)

questions.q: Which structure does the duration table name as the storage site for short-term/recent memory?
questions.exp: Storage row: immediate = no storage; short term/recent = hippocampus (medial temporal lobe); long term = neocortex - and retrieval in all three columns is the prefrontal cortex. (Book p569)

questions.q: The current classification splits memory by mode of retrieval into which two branches?
questions.exp: Mode of retrieval (current classifications): explicit (declarative) - episodic and semantic - and implicit (non-declaratives): procedural, priming, associative (conditional), non associative. (Book p569)

questions.q: Episodic memory per the flowchart is based on time and context (autobiographical), is hippocampal, and is affected early in which disease?
questions.exp: Episodic: based on time and context (autobiographical), area hippocampus, affected early in Alzheimer's disease; semantic: based on facts, association areas, rarely affected in late Alzheimer's disease. (Book p569)

questions.q: Pick the ODD ONE OUT - the type NOT listed under implicit (non-declarative) memory:
questions.exp: Implicit (non-declaratives) listed: procedural, priming, associative (conditional) and non associative; episodic belongs to explicit (declarative) memory. (Book p569)

questions.q: Per the implicit-memory table, procedural memory (e.g. driving) uses which areas?
opts: Basal ganglia, supplementary motor area and cerebellum
questions.exp: Procedural: basal ganglia, supplementary motor area, cerebellum (e.g. driving); priming: neo cortex (remembering facts d/t exposure, duration or intensity); associative (conditional): amygdala (not seen in humans - animals associating fear to lion and environment); non-associative: reflex pathway (habitual response). (Book p570)

questions.q: An animal's fear-association response to a predator in its environment is mapped in the table to which area?
questions.exp: Associative (conditional) memory: amygdala; characteristics - not seen in humans; animals associating fear to lion and environment. (Book p570)

questions.q: Per the cortex anatomy table, which lobe's area stores semantic memory?
questions.exp: Cortex table: frontal (prefrontal cortex, all types), parietal (association area parieto-occipital, semantic), temporal (hippocampus, episodic semantic), occipital (area '-', semantic). (Book p570)

questions.q: Which subcortical area is labelled the 'gateway of memory' storing long-term memory?
questions.exp: Sub-cortex table: amygdala -> conditional; cerebellum -> procedural; entorhinal cortex -> long term memory (gateway of memory); basal ganglia -> procedural. The zones-of-brain medial diagram follows. (Book p570)

questions.q: The Papez circuit is also known as what, and which station is annotated with Wernicke-Korsakoff syndromes?
questions.exp: Papez circuit aka mammillo-thalamic circuit: hippocampus/subiculum -> fornix -> mammillary body (Wernicke-Korsakoff syndromes) -> mammillo-thalamic tract -> thalamus -> internal capsule -> cingulate gyrus -> parahippocampal gyrus -> entorhinal cortex (gateway of memory) -> back to hippocampus. (Book p571)

questions.q: In the Papez circuit, which station is the 'gateway of memory' that closes the loop back to the hippocampus?
questions.exp: The circuit closes via the parahippocampal gyrus into the entorhinal cortex, labelled gateway of memory, which returns to the hippocampus/subiculum. (Book p571)

units.title: 1. Processes & Classification
units.guide:
Three processes (encoding, consolidation, retrieval) precede the old duration table.
The current classification splits explicit vs implicit memory, with episodic/semantic branches.

units.title: 2. Implicit Memory & Anatomy
units.guide:
The implicit-memory table pairs each type with its areas and characteristics.
The cortex and sub-cortex anatomy tables then assign memory types to lobes and nuclei.

units.title: 3. Papez Circuit
units.guide:
The mammillo-thalamic circuit is traced station by station.
The mammillary body carries the Wernicke-Korsakoff annotation; the entorhinal cortex closes the loop.
